A 62-year-old man presents to the emergency department with increased fatigue and changes in his vision.
There are large, non-tender palpable lymph nodes in the patient's inguinal region.
A neurological exam is notable for decreased sensation in the patient's hands and feet.
The dermatologic exam is notable for multiple bruises on his upper and lower extremities.
His temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 157/98 mmHg, pulse is 90/min, respirations are 17/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air.
The patient also endorses increased sweating at night and new-onset headaches.
He also complains of numbness and tingling pain in his extremities that has been persistent during this time.
Abdominal exam reveals splenomegaly and hepatomegaly.
A cardiopulmonary exam is within normal limits.
The patient has a medical history of diabetes and hypertension.
His current medications include insulin, metformin, and lisinopril.
For the past month, he has felt abnormally tired and today noticed his vision is blurry.
